title: Server Commands From Chat
tagline: Ops from your pocket — with seatbelts
script: Running server commands from a chat app sounds like a security incident waiting to happen. So here's what actually happens when IronClaw runs one. First, the environment: the agent's shell doesn't inherit yours. It's wiped and rebuilt from a short allowlist — no keys, no tokens, no secrets, because nothing survives unless it's explicitly named. Second, every command is screened before it runs: destructive patterns, downloads piped into a shell, exfiltration tricks like DNS tunneling and netcat pipes, reads of sensitive paths like your SSH keys — refused. Third, the output comes back through a leak detector, so a stray secret in a log never reaches the model. And the blast radius is yours to set: runtime profiles decide whether the agent touches a sandbox or a real host. Ask for the disk usage from your phone. Convenience without the blast radius.

claims.text: shell wiped and rebuilt from a short allowlist — nothing survives unless named
every command screened before it runs — destructive patterns, pipe-to-shell, exfiltration, sensitive paths
output scrubbed of credential shapes before the model sees it
